rules.title: Drop-required iff own Drop or droppable field
rules.statement: A type needs drop glue iff it has a user/own drop function OR it transitively contains at least one droppable field (needs_drop(t) = own_drop(t) ∨ has_droppable_fields(t)).

rules.title: Move propagates into composite producer subexpressions
rules.statement: When a value is produced from a composite expression (Call arg, StructLit field, TupleLit elem, EnumLitData payload, BlockExpr result), any move-typed VarRef carried into the produced value is marked moved and removed from the drop set; FieldRead in producer position is a move of the source. This prevents double-drop / use-after-move for values escaping via construction.

rules.title: break/continue runs drops down to enclosing loop body
rules.statement: A `break`/`continue` runs the destructors of every scope frame from the innermost enclosing frame down to and including the enclosing loop-body frame, so a break/continue nested inside an `if` still drops the loop body's locals.

rules.title: Or-pattern alternatives share one slot per binding name
rules.statement: Within a single top-level pattern, a binding name introduced in multiple Or-pattern alternatives (`Some(x) | Other(x)`) resolves to ONE shared storage slot; the slot is reserved at build time and the build-local name→slot map is cleared at each top-level pattern entry.

rules.title: Location-anchored types may not occupy a by-value slot
rules.statement: A non-movable (location-anchored) type — one with a self-relative `#[rel_ptr]`/`#[zoned2]` field, or a `#[pinned]` type — may not be bound to any by-value slot (let local, parameter, match/for/closure/destructure binding); it must live behind a pointer, in place (e.g. an arena or `[u8;N]` buffer), and be built through a `*mut T`.
rules.divergence:
A8: `#[pinned]` is non-movability as a property of the TYPE (no value-form), distinct from Rust's pointer-level Pin

.

rules.title: Each binding gets a fresh slot; shadowing allocates a new slot
rules.statement: Each binding occupies a fresh dense slot allocated at definition; re-declaring a name in the same/inner scope (shadowing) allocates a new slot rather than reusing the prior one (unless a pattern pre-reserved a slot for an Or-alternative).

rules.title: Name resolution: innermost binding wins, then module consts
rules.statement: A name resolves to its innermost in-scope local binding (shadowing-correct); if no local binding exists it falls back to a module-level const; otherwise it is unresolved.

rules.title: Passing an owning Box<dyn Trait> by value moves it
rules.statement: An owning `Box<dyn Trait>` binding (collapsed to a bare trait object) is moved when passed by value — the callee frees the handle — so the caller marks it moved to avoid a double-free.

rules.title: Struct with a zoned-struct field is not plain data
rules.statement: A struct is plain-data (is_data_plain) unless any of its fields has zoned-struct kind, in which case it is a (non-plain) zoned datatype.

rules.title: Tuple struct: positional fields, call-form ctor and pattern
rules.statement: `struct Foo(T1, T2);` declares a tuple struct with positional fields; its constructor is the call form `Foo(a, b)` and its pattern is `Foo(x, y)`.

rules.title: #[no_auto_drop] suppresses compiler-emitted drop
rules.statement: A struct marked `#[no_auto_drop]` receives NO compiler-emitted automatic Drop (neither user-drop invocation nor field drop glue) — the ManuallyDrop<T> lang-item shape.

rules.title: Trailing unsized field makes the struct a custom DST
rules.statement: A struct whose LAST field has unsized type (`[T]`, `dyn Trait`, or nested DST) is itself unsized (is_dst); such a struct may appear only behind `&`/`&mut`/`*const`/`*mut`/`Box`, and is constructed via unsafe raw-parts assembly (never by value).

rules.title: #[self_describing] custom-DST uses a thin raw pointer
rules.statement: A custom-DST struct marked `#[self_describing]` has in-band recoverable tail length/metadata, so raw `*const T`/`*mut T` to it is a THIN pointer (metadata recovered at deref) rather than a fat DstRef.

rules.title: #[rel_ptr] field stored as self-relative i64 offset
rules.statement: A `#[rel_ptr]` field is stored as an 8-byte i64 byte-offset from the field's own address and materializes to an absolute thin pointer on load; it is opaque (no field access) but transparent to `*Pointee` at the value level.

rules.title: #[pinned] type is location-anchored and non-movable
rules.statement: A `#[pinned]` type's bits are anchored to its storage slot: it must not be moved by value, is accessed in place, and is materialized to a movable value form only explicitly. It is non-movable itself (unlike `#[rel_ptr]`, whose value form is the resolved absolute pointer).

rules.title: #[zone_mut] gives &mut T a zone-carrying fat ref
rules.statement: For a `#[zone_mut]` type, `&mut T` is a fat reference {data, zone=*mut Allocator} carrying its zone so grow methods can reach the allocator from `&mut self`; a read `&T` stays thin.

rules.title: #[zoned2] stores all thin-pointer fields self-relative
rules.statement: A `#[zoned2]` struct stores all of its thin-pointer fields as self-relative RelOffset i64 and materializes them to absolute pointers in compute; such a struct is non-movable (it cannot be stack-allocated because the offsets are anchored to the slot).

rules.title: #[borrow_carrying] values escape-tracked like references
rules.statement: A `#[borrow_carrying]` value type may contain an absolute Ref into an arena; the borrow checker tracks its escape like a reference — a method/ctor returning one ties the result to its ref receiver/arg, so returning it past the source's scope is rejected unless laundered through a holder.

rules.title: #[non_null] enables Option NullPtr niche
rules.statement: A `#[non_null]` struct is a single 8-byte pointer wrapper whose pointer is guaranteed non-null (Box/Rc/Arc shape), letting `Option<ThisStruct>` use the NullPtr niche (None = null pointer, pointer-sized enum). It is an opt-in soundness contract asserted by the author.

rules.title: union layout and unsafe field read
rules.statement: A type declared `union NAME { … }` has layout = max-of-fields size aligned to max field alignment (vs struct's sum-of-fields); only one field is active at a time (the active one is implementation-defined) and every field READ requires an enclosing `unsafe`.

rules.title: #[repr(transparent)] inherits the single field's layout
rules.statement: A single-field wrapper marked `#[repr(transparent)]` inherits its field's layout exactly (size, align, and niche). Other `#[repr(...)]` modes (`C`/`packed`/`align`) are parsed then rejected.

rules.title: Enum default discriminant backing type is i32
rules.statement: An enum with no explicit backing type uses i32 as its discriminant backing type.

rules.title: Struct-shape enum variant carries named payload fields
rules.statement: An enum variant `V { x: T, y: U }` is a struct-shape variant with named payload fields (a names array parallel to payload types); user-written field names are resolved to positional indices. Tuple-shape and unit variants carry no payload field names.

rules.title: where Self: Sized method excluded from vtable
rules.statement: A trait method with `where Self: Sized` is excluded from the trait's vtable and ignored for object-safety determination.

rules.title: Conditional default methods gated by per-method param bounds
rules.statement: A per-method `where` bound whose subject is a trait type-parameter (e.g. `where Item: Ord`) gates default-method synthesis per impl: when an impl substitutes the type-parameter, the bound is rewritten under the substitution and checked; if unsatisfied, the default method is not synthesized for that impl (the method is simply unavailable).

rules.title: Associated types may be generic (GAT) and have a default
rules.statement: A trait associated type may carry its own type-params (`type Item<T>` — a GAT) with bounds, and may declare a default (`type Item = i32;`) used by impls that omit it.

rules.title: Associated const default projected into omitting impls
rules.statement: A trait associated const may declare a default (`const X: i32 = 42;`); each `impl Trait for T` that omits the const inherits the default so `T::CONST` resolves to it.

rules.title: Negative impl asserts a type does not implement a trait
rules.statement: `impl !Trait for X {}` is a negative impl declaring that X does not implement Trait.

rules.title: Trait may declare supertrait bounds
rules.statement: A trait declaration `trait Foo: Display + Into<i32>` records supertrait bounds (trait name + type-args) that every impl of Foo must also satisfy.

rules.title: Distinct trait type-args coexist via mangled method keys
rules.statement: Two impls of the same trait name for one type at distinct trait type-args (`impl Trait<u64> for X` vs `impl Trait<u32> for X`) mangle their methods by the impl's concrete trait type-args so the methods coexist and dispatch independently.

rules.title: Colliding trait methods re-keyed under trait-qualified name
rules.statement: When two traits define the same method on the same target type and signature, the colliding methods are re-keyed under the trait-qualified base `<target>__<trait>__<method>` to disambiguate.

rules.title: ! fallback for unbound type-param of always-diverging callee
rules.statement: If a callee's body always diverges (panic-tail or `loop {}`-tail) and a type-parameter is otherwise unbound at the call site, the inference variable falls back to `!` (Never). A non-diverging body leaves an unbound type-param as an ambiguity error: `fn f<T>()->T{panic();}` infers T=! while `fn f<T>()->T{return 0;}` is ambiguous.

rules.title: name!(...) resolves only #[fn_macro]/#[token_macro] callees
rules.statement: A function-style macro call `name!(...)` resolves only callees marked `#[fn_macro]`; a `#[token_macro]` callee additionally receives its raw source text directly as a `str` argument.

rules.title: pub(module) exports within the owning module only
rules.statement: An item marked `pub(module)` is exported within its owning module only (module-linkage: visibility crosses package boundaries inside the same module) but is not visible to external consumers; `pub(module)` implies `pub` at the package level.
